insights: Through two graded days Claude is 20-10 (+$196 on $10 stakes) and the formula is 4-5 (-$10). Friday was a losing night: Claude 4-10 (-$68), mostly because one upset (Pistons lost to Toronto by 3) was sitting in five different bets, and the Rockets underdog pick was in four more. What held up: singles (10-2), underdogs with points (4-0, Wyoming and the Kings both covered) and unders (2-0). What did not: every prop parlay lost (0-5) even though the individual prop legs went 20-6, because each 6-leg ticket missed by one leg. Today: no team goes in more than two new bets, the safer prop parlay is cut to 2 legs, no moneyline underdogs, and only one 4+ leg long shot (already posted). It is still a small sample (about 30 different results), so treat these as leanings, not proof.

working: Underdogs getting points (4-0: Rice, Wyoming, Kings +14.5, plus Saint Mary's -1.5)
Individual prop legs, especially unders (14-3 across both pickers)
NBA and college hoops favorites for the formula (18-3 legs)
notWorking: Putting the same team in many bets (Pistons loss sank 5 bets, Rockets 4)
6-leg prop parlays (0-4, each missed by one leg)
Formula favorites in the -140 to -180 range (Temple, NC State both lost)
rules: Sample is two nights (about 30 different results): do not raise stakes or leg counts because of it
No team in more than 2 new bets per day, so one upset cannot sink the card
Parlay legs must be picks I would bet as singles; no -1000 filler
At most one 4+ leg long shot per day
No moneyline underdogs in parlays; take underdogs with points instead
Props: the safer parlay is 2 legs, lean to unders; 5-6 leg prop parlays are always Long shot
Formula: only favorites -150 or stronger go into formula parlays; also post a 2-leg version of the prop parlay
